title: exists strictPerfect upper model
statement:
Let E be a site-perfect derived object of module sheaves over a commutative ring sheaf R. If its cohomology vanishes in all degrees above b, then over every object U there is a covering sieve whose arrows V→U admit bounded strict-perfect representatives of E restricted to V with every term above b zero. The sheafification and derived-category hypotheses and independent universes are as displayed below.

Precise quantified statement:
theorem exists_strictPerfect_upper_model
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [∀ U : C, HasSheafify (J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [∀ U : C, (J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max u v})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{max u v}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R))]
    [∀ U : C, HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (SheafOfModules.{max u v}
      (((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R).over U))]
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R)))
    (hperfect : IsPerfectOnRingedSiteOfUniverses.{u, v, 0} R E)
    (b : ℤ)
    (hcoh : ∀ r : ℤ, b < r →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ r).obj E)) :
    ∀ U : C, ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ J U ∧
      ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
        ∃ P : StrictPerfectCoefficientRepresentationOfUniverses.{u, v, 0} R V
          (ringedSiteDerivedRestrictionOfUniverses
            ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{max u v} RingCat.{max u v})).obj R) V E),
          ∀ r : ℤ, b < r → IsZero (P.F.X r)

proof.text: Start on a strict-perfect chart. By descending induction from a term bound, construct locally finite-free retractions for cycles: exactness makes the map onto the next cycles epic, local finite-projective lifting splits it, and 1-fs factors through the kernel. Compose the finite covering refinements. The good upper truncation at b has these cycles in degree b, unchanged lower terms and zero higher terms. Its canonical map is a quasi-isomorphism since cohomology vanishes above b. Exact restriction and the successive restriction comparisons identify its derived object with the required restriction of E.
